models.title: Unit contribution margin
models.summary: The bottle-cap example subtracts variable cost per unit from selling price per unit.

relationship.original_equation: Unit contribution margin = unit selling price − unit variable cost
relationship.translation_notes: Inputs and output are currency per unit.

variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship
Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship
Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Unit price and variable cost refer to the same product, currency and activity basis.
The cost classification is appropriate over the relevant activity range.
limitations: A negative contribution is possible when variable unit cost exceeds price.
Contribution margin is not the same as gross profit under absorption costing.

models.title: Operating profit from total contribution and fixed costs
models.summary: The restaurant example deducts fixed costs from the contribution remaining after variable costs.

relationship.original_equation: Operating profit = total contribution margin − fixed operating costs
relationship.translation_notes: The output and contribution are signed amounts; fixed costs are nonnegative.

assumptions: Contribution and fixed operating costs use the same reporting period and operating scope.
All relevant operating costs are classified exactly once as variable or fixed.
limitations: Operating profit can be negative and excludes interest and tax in this simplified analysis.
The owner example mistakenly prints 50,000 in one subtraction; its stated fixed cost and result support 250,000.

relationship.original_equation: Selling price = cost × (1 + markup on cost)

relationship.translation_notes: Markup is a base-one fraction and 1 is the identity multiplier on cost.
